_doc: BINARY WIRE -- the byte-level codec gate, shared by both active ports.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every OTHER codec gate in this repository compares
canonical test-JSON STRINGS, and the fields the binary codec drops are a
strict SUBSET of the fields that string oracle also drops (measured; see
test_fixtures/expected/codec_field_survival.json and coverage gap
`codec-string-oracle-cannot-see-a-dropped-field`). So no fixture could
NOTE 2026-07-28: that SUBSET claim was true when ruled and is NOT true now --
the preservation wave extended canonical test-JSON to carry all twelve
formerly-dropped fields, so test_json drops NOTHING and binary dropped
fill_gradient and stroke_gradient until 2026-11-12 (I1b: now carried). The oracle got STRONGER. This gate stays:
it is BYTE-level where the oracle is string-level, a different question.
red-light a binary drop, and a one-port slot mismatch in `pack_element` /
`packElement` would land SILENTLY. Extending a format whose divergences we
cannot see is not acceptable, so this gate was RULED to land in the same
wave as the per-tag trailing extension (2026-07-27, see
transcripts/EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md).
WHAT MAKES IT A CROSS-PORT STATEMENT. There is ONE golden here, not a
mirrored literal per port. A port that drifts cannot fix itself by editing
its own copy, because it has no copy: it must move the shared file, which
immediately reds the other port. That is the property the two mirrored
DONUT_*_HEX literals in binary.rs / BinaryFillRuleTests.swift did NOT have.
WHAT IT DOES NOT WATCH. It compares what the WRITERS produce for documents
each port CONSTRUCTS IN CODE (`wire_case_document` in
jas_dioxus/src/cross_language_test.rs, `wireCaseDocument` in
JasSwift/Tests/CrossLanguageTests.swift). Those two constructions are part
of what is being compared, so they must stay shape-for-shape identical; a
case whose two constructors drift apart would fail loudly, but a case whose
constructors are BOTH wrong about the intent would pass. It says nothing
about the READ path beyond the fact that each pinned blob still decodes,
and nothing about whether a field survives -- that is
codec_field_survival.json's job. Neither gate subsumes the other.
`tag_arity` -- the number of msgpack slots the writer emits for each
element tag, asserted through `packed_element_slot_count` /
`packedElementSlotCount`. The per-tag trailing append is DEFINED against
these numbers: `unpack_common` reads FIXED indices 1..6 and every variant's
payload starts at index 7, so the shared common block could not be extended
once and each tag's extension block begins at the tag's own base arity
(arity minus the extension). Both ports carry the same `tag_base_arity`
table; this file is the third, language-neutral copy that makes a drift
between them visible.
`cases[].hex` -- the UNCOMPRESSED blob, byte for byte, so the pinned string
is the msgpack itself and not a deflate stream. Regenerate after an
INTENTIONAL codec change with
`cargo test print_binary_wire_hex -- --ignored --nocapture` and paste the
result here; the swift lane then reds until it agrees, which is the point.
`cases[].port_hex` -- a case where the two ports MEASURABLY DISAGREE today.
`hex` is what both ports must eventually reach; a port named here is
asserted to produce the stated OTHER bytes, so CLOSING the divergence reds
this gate until the entry is deleted. A divergence can therefore never rot
into a silent suppression (the same discipline as `port_overrides` in
codec_field_survival.json and `expected_violations` in
test_fixtures/preservation/). Empty is the goal state.
_tag_arity_doc: tag -> packed slot count. Base arity (the index the extension block starts at) is this number minus 3 -- and minus 5 for `path`, which also carries stroke_brush + stroke_brush_overrides, and for `layer` and `group`, which since 2026-07-28 also carry isolated_blending + knockout_group at the SAME two offsets (a tag holds the path pair or the container pair, never both). Kept OUTSIDE `tag_arity` so the gate can assert that it reaches every declared key -- a comment inside the map would read as a thirteenth tag.

cases.name: shapes_default
cases._doc: One Group, Line, Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Polyline, Polygon and Path at their defaults inside one Layer. Minimal content on purpose: arity is a property of the tag, not of the values, so fewer numbers keeps the bytes readable. Byte-identical in both ports.

cases.name: text_default
cases._doc: A default Text and a default TextPath. Kept as its own case because the TSPAN payload is where this gate scored its first hit: on 2026-07-27, the moment it existed, it measured jas_dioxus writing FIFTY-ONE slots per tspan (array header 0x33) against JasSwift writing TWENTY-TWO (0x16), so at that commit the two ports did NOT write the same bytes for any Text or TextPath (measured; whether they ever did is a history question nobody drove) and JasSwift silently dropped 29 tspan fields on a round trip although its own Tspan struct held every one. Invisible to every pre-existing gate for exactly the ruled reason: the codec gates compare canonical test-JSON strings, binary_read_python_fixtures reads PYTHON-written bytes, and both ports read trailing slots tolerantly, so each round-tripped its OWN blobs and neither noticed the other. It was pinned here as port_hex.swift and then CLOSED in the same wave by mirroring Rust field order into packTspan / unpackTspan -- and the entry had to be DELETED to get this gate green again, which is the pinning discipline doing its job. The 0x33 header below is what both ports now write.

cases.name: live_default
cases._doc: All four LIVE kinds (compound_shape, reference, recorded, generated), which share one tag and therefore one arity.

cases.name: saturated_extension
cases._doc: The extension's whole reason for existing, at non-default values: `codec_field_survival.json`'s saturated Path -- masked, blend-moded, tool-tagged, brushed, even-odd, with a width profile and both arrowheads. Its two gradients ride the last two slots of every tag as canonical test-JSON text (I1b, 2026-11-12); before that day they were NOT on the wire, and this is the case whose bytes moved.
